edges.effect_quant: In the best direct young-women trial, ferritin improvement tracked with a 5-fold to 7-fold improvement in cognitive performance accuracy, and later randomized iron interventions also improved attention and memory tasks relative to control conditions.
edges.mechanism: Iron supports myelination, mitochondrial energy production, and dopamine-dependent attention and processing-speed pathways. Repleting low iron stores can therefore improve task accuracy or speed even when the cognitive effect is modest rather than dramatic.
edges.summary: Randomized trials suggest that correcting low iron status can improve selected aspects of cognition, especially attention, processing speed, and some memory tasks in iron-depleted people. The evidence is strongest in women of reproductive age and other high-risk groups, with benefits present but not universal across every cognitive domain.
edges.caveats: The literature is heterogeneous in age, baseline anemia severity, and the cognitive tests used. Some supportive trials use iron fortification rather than tablets, so the edge is best read as benefit from iron repletion in low-iron states rather than from any one product form.
